title: Gospel temporal sequence
subtitle: Build the scene, then follow the events.
overview: Narrative Greek commonly uses imperfect forms for setting or ongoing activity and aorist forms for events viewed as wholes in the storyline.
This is a reading heuristic, not an automatic translation machine: lexical meaning and discourse context always matter.

items.grc: καὶ ἦν διδάσκων αὐτούς, καὶ ἦλθεν πρὸς αὐτὸν λεπρός.
items.en: And he was teaching them, and a leper came to him.
And he said to him, “I am willing; be cleansed.”
